citation.title: Populating cellular metamaterials on the extrema of attainable elasticity through neuroevolution
citation.authors: Maohua Yan; Ruicheng Wang; Ke Liu
citation.venue: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 440, 117950
citation.version_coded: latest accessible arXiv version; version of record is not open

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: For orthotropic metamaterials, neuroevolution produces a dense, uniformly populated Pareto front, whereas the cited topology-optimization-driven results provide sparse points.
claim.key_phrase: uniformly and densely located on the Pareto front
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No comparative runtime or speed-up is reported for the proposed method.
claim.alternatives: Section 3.3 reports that after 800 iterations the three property-pair outcomes are consistent with Ref. [5]; the abstract describes efficient exploration but gives no classical timing comparison.

baseline.classical_method: Topology-optimization-driven metamaterial design cited in Section 3.3, Ref. [5]
baseline.hardware_ml: Alibaba Cloud machine: AMD EPYC 7H12, 256 CPU processors at 2.60 GHz, 503 GiB DDR4 RAM; GPU not used (Section 3.3)
baseline.problem_size: 2D periodic metamaterial unit cells; high-resolution point clouds (exact resolution not stated in the cited comparison)
baseline.training_time: not stated; authors state method uses no prior data
baseline.quality_metric: homogenized elastic properties and Pareto-front coverage
baseline.quality_gap: Cited topology-optimization-driven work is described as yielding sparse Pareto-front points while the proposed method populates the front densely (Section 3.3); no numeric gap stated.

R1.evidence: The stated comparison concerns Pareto-front coverage and elastic properties, not speed.

R2.evidence: Section 3.3 gives no compared runtime; no classical hardware or solver details are provided.

R3.evidence: The primary comparison is design quality; no speed claim for the proposed method is quantified.

R4.evidence: Sections 2–3 evaluate generated designs using FEM-based computational homogenization and report elastic properties, but do not report failed or infeasible design rates.

reporting.n_test_cases: Four material symmetry cases: isotropic, tetragonal, orthotropic, and fully anisotropic (Sections 3.1–3.4)

notes: The version of record is paywalled; coded the accessible arXiv text.
